summary: Amplifier classes, FM and SSB math, matching networks, and keeping a transmitter's signal clean.

blocks.title: Amplifier basics
items: Cutoff: fully off. Saturation: fully on. Between them is the linear region.
Bias: where the device rests with no signal.

blocks.title: Conduction by class
blocks.caption: Blue: conducting. Grey: cut off. Dot: bias. Dashed: cutoff.

head: Class

blocks.title: Using the classes
items: Class C's pulses ring a tuned tank circuit, restoring a sine wave.
Class C suits CW and FM, not SSB: it's too nonlinear.
Judge Class A signal handling by peak voltage: peaks can clip.

blocks.title: Modulation
items: AM varies the carrier's strength, FM its frequency, PM its phase.

blocks.title: Single sideband
items: Sidebands: carrier plus and minus audio. Each holds all the voice.
To make SSB, cancel the carrier and filter the unwanted sideband: a balanced modulator followed by a filter.
A non-linear amplifier causes distortion: intermodulation products and splatter.
PEP, peak envelope power: power at the envelope's highest point. PEP to average is about 2.5 to 1, set by speech characteristics.

items.name: DC input power
items.means: Class AB RF linear amp: about 50%.

items.name: PEP from a scope
items.example: 200 V peak-to-peak = 100 V peak = 70.7 V RMS; 5,000 ÷ 50 Ω ≈ 100 W

blocks.title: Clean signals
items: Even-order harmonics: a push-pull amplifier cancels them. Push-push reinforces them: a frequency doubler.

Intermodulation interference: 2 nearby transmitters' signals mix in one or both final amplifiers, making sum and difference frequencies. Cure: a terminated circulator or ferrite isolator in the feed line to the transmitter and duplexer.
Spread spectrum: wide-bandwidth; the RF carrier varies by a pre-determined sequence, frequency hopping 1 or multiple carriers.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: DC input, multiplied by mistake: 250 W.
Forget to double in Carson's rule: 8 kHz.
Filters don't stop intermodulation: the other signal often passes them.
